FIND: CONFIRM C0206 with verified fix. `build_feedback_records()` section 4 iterates `rk_validation` as `for model_id, validation_records in rk_validation.items()` but never uses `model_id`. The `fid` from each validation record is looked up in `finding_by_id` (which spans all models), so a validation record keyed under model A could be applied to a finding produced by model B if both share the same `fid`. The feedback record would then carry model B's `model_origin` but model A's R_k data.

FOLLOW: Downstream, `build_feedback_sections` groups records by `model_origin`. The cross-applied R_k discrepancy would appear in model B's feedback section, telling model B its R_k is wrong when it was model A's validation that flagged the issue. Model B would receive a `RECALIBRATE_RK` action for a discrepancy it didn't cause.

ANALYSE: HARD constraint (correctness). Premises: (1) `rk_validation` is keyed by `model_id` (per docstring: `Dict[model_id, List[...]]`). (2) The outer loop binds `model_id` but never references it. (3) `finding_by_id` is a flat dict across all models. (4) `finding.model_id` may differ from the outer `model_id`. Conclusion: cross-model R_k misattribution is possible whenever two models' validation records reference findings with overlapping IDs. CONFIRMED.

FIND: CONFIRM C0230 with verified fix. `build_feedback_records()` section 1 iterates only `cell_verdicts.items()`. A finding that appears in `final_verdicts` as `"REJECTED"` but has no entry in `cell_verdicts` (no specialist cell evaluated it) will never enter `records_by_id`. The `if refutations or final_v == "REJECTED"` guard on line ~253 only fires for findings already in `cell_verdicts`.

FOLLOW: Such a finding receives zero corrective feedback in round K+1. The model that produced it sees no schema signal and may resubmit it unchanged, violating the feedback channel's core contract (§17: models MUST address flagged findings). The finding is silently approved from the model's perspective despite being pipeline-REJECTED.

ANALYSE: HARD constraint (correctness). Premises: (1) `cell_verdicts` is populated by specialist immune cells. (2) `final_verdicts` is the pipeline-level aggregation. (3) A finding can be REJECTED at pipeline level without any individual cell issuing a REJECTED verdict (e.g., insufficient evidence from all cells leads to pipeline-level rejection). (4) The section 1 loop's entry condition is `for fid, verdict_list in cell_verdicts.items()` — unreachable for findings not in `cell_verdicts`. CONFIRMED.
